I'd call 19 households before 15 April 2026: five whose 401(k) RMD was never paid, five who skipped an inherited-IRA RMD, five whose backdoor Roth conversion is partly taxable, and four with a wash sale. No household has more than one problem, and the files settle every case, so nothing is left unresolved.

**RMD not met: 401(k) share paid from an IRA (HH-0120, HH-0236, HH-0371, HH-0664, HH-5271).** Each owner turned 73 in 2025 and is a former employee with a 401(k). Each took one combined payment covering the IRAs and the 401(k), paid from an IRA. IRA RMDs can be combined that way, but a 401(k)'s RMD must come out of the 401(k) itself. So each 401(k)'s RMD (about $11,000–$15,000) was not met, and the 1 April 2026 deadline has passed. Each combined payment equals the 31 Dec 2024 balance of all three accounts ÷ 26.5, the standard IRS divisor at age 73 (it isn't in the files).

**RMD not met: inherited IRAs (HH-0607, HH-0466, HH-7126, HH-0491, HH-0842).** In each, the original owner died after RMDs had started, and the CRM shows the prior custodian confirming that. The heirs are adult children, so annual RMDs are due, and 2025 is the first year the penalty relief no longer covers. None of these accounts paid out anything in 2025. I didn't calculate the missed amounts because the life-expectancy divisors aren't in the files. The five inherited IRAs whose owners died before starting RMDs (HH-7683, 0571, 0330, 0328, 0716) owe nothing for 2025.

**Backdoor Roth partly taxable (HH-0218, HH-0844, HH-0347, HH-0690, HH-1204).** Each converter still had a pre-tax rollover IRA on 31 Dec 2025, and none had any recorded basis. Under the pro-rata rule only about $205–$327 of each conversion is tax-free, leaving roughly $6,700–$7,700 taxable. The other five backdoor households (0799, 0608, 0747, 0633, 1587) keep their pre-tax money only in a 401(k), which doesn't count, so they have no surprise.

**Wash sales (HH-0129, HH-0363, HH-9234, HH-0780).** Each couple sold at a loss in their joint account. Then, 12–28 days later, the same fund was bought in one spouse's IRA. In HH-0129 the purchase went into a Roth IRA, so the disallowed part of the loss is lost for good. Four other sales missed the 30-day window by days: HH-9571 (31 days), HH-0380 (35), HH-0981 (37) and HH-0847 (41). The RSU sales either had no new shares vesting within 30 days, or (HH-3058) were gains once the vest prices in the CRM are used as cost basis.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which households should we call before 15 April 2026 about a 2025 tax or distribution surprise, and why?

Count three kinds of surprise, and no other:
- "backdoor_roth_taxed": a 2025 contribution to a traditional IRA converted to a Roth IRA in 2025, part of which is taxable under the pro-rata rule because the person's traditional IRAs held pre-tax money on 31 December 2025;
- "rmd_not_met": a 2025 required minimum distribution, from any retirement account, that was not met;
- "wash_sale": a 2025 sale at a loss in a taxable account, with the same security acquired within 30 days before or after it in an account of the seller or the seller's spouse, so that some of the loss is a wash sale.

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more households had such a surprise, "none_found" if none did, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household to call, each as {"household_id": ..., "surprises": the kinds above that apply, "person_ids": the person each surprise concerns (who converted, whose RMD was not met), "account_ids": the accounts an unmet RMD had to come from, "transaction_ids": the backdoor Roth's conversion, and the wash sale's loss sales and the acquisitions that replace them, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on from the files, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed from them rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
